segmentation.text: When a vehicle
enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered,
but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop, the driver shall proceed cautiously, yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', never expanded into classes.

The entry is the observation at which the subject's footprint begins to overlap the intersection: rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' on st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', the defined word's whole extent (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'); not a crosswalk or stop line, which are other regions.

dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head' with the 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered', which is the words 'installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered'. 'Controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection': the head governs the intersection or a carrier whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; carriers quantified as st.travel_region). Not a position: governance, not where the halt is.
dev.inoperative 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication' is 'inoperative'; read at the entry observation, the moment the words fix ('at the time the vehicle enters').

The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (ontology section 9); the class is the vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. ru.aggregate's exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives' does not apply: the atom is claimed for the vehicle, not for the driver role.

Proceeding as at a stop sign at the entrance the subject uses is the halt the words go on to place: 'stop' when required is DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement' (drv.motion.stopped), made while x occupies (rel.occupies) its approach carrier (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters). The place, in order: st.stop_line 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device' recorded as marking the carrier (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'); else st.crosswalk 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection' marking it, the halt made before the footprint overlaps it; else the carrier's entrance end at st.intersection, with the footprint outside it. At the place is within the stop-point tolerance of it (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), on its upstream side read along the carrier's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along 'the signed distance ... measured along a carrier's designated direction'). Not the distance to a signal head (dev.position).

operationalizations.standard: has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway
operationalizations.convention: The view of approaching traffic on the through highway is a sight distance along that way, st.sight_along_way 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye', at least the stopping sight distance of the approach-speed design convention (AASHTO stopping sight distance). The through highway is a st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') that the intersection lies on (st.on_way 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there') and the subject's approach carrier does not.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The rule is judged at each entry of x into an intersection i: an observation at which x's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) and at the observation before did not. It applies where, at that entry observation, at least one traffic signal head d (dev.traffic_signal, installed and uncovered) controls i - d governs i itself, or governs a carrier c whose entrance end is i (dev.governs, st.lane_enters) - and every such head that governs i or x's approach carrier is inoperative (dev.inoperative) at that observation.
obligation: Event: the entry of x into i defined in the applicability. Approach: the carrier c (st.travel_region) x occupies at the observation before the entry whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters c i); where x occupies several such carriers and the verdict differs between them, unknown. Place, in the words' order: (1) a stop line s recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of s c); (2) where the stop-line association of c is observed and lists none, a crosswalk w recorded as marking c, the halt made before x's footprint overlaps w; (3) where neither is recorded for c (associations observed), the entrance end of c at i: a halt with x's footprint outside i, within p.stop_point_tolerance of i, at an observation at which the sight along a through highway h (a st.highway that i lies on and c does not, st.on_way) is at least p.approach_view_sight_distance (st.sight_along_way from x to h). Act: drv.motion.stopped(x) with param p.motion_speed_tolerance at an observation at which x is on c, outside i, on the upstream side of the place (prim.region_offset_along along c's designated direction not past it, a halt on the line counting) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry distance between x's body and the place); for a crosswalk, also with x's footprint not overlapping it. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start - the last observation before the entry at which x, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance) - or at x's previous entry into i through the same place, whichever is later. A crossing of the mark, a change of carrier within the same entry, a lateral move or speed noise begins no new approach. The duty is met where the search finds the act, violated where it reaches either end without the act, and unknown only where it reaches neither (the recording begins inside the stopping zone with no act recorded). Whether the entry occurred is unknown where the observation before does not place x on a mapped carrier with an observed association to the place; where c's association with a stop line or crosswalk, c's direction or a needed sight distance is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown, never decided from a distance alone.

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'Clearly marked' is read as the stop line the scene represents; paint clarity is not modelled.

'The point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view' is read as the entrance end of the approach carrier (outside the intersection, within the stop-point tolerance) at which the view bound is met; a halt farther upstream does not count. 'Proceed as if a stop sign had been erected' is read through the halt the words go on to place; the yield a stop sign also entails is the sibling node's duty.
The driver's view is read as what could be seen from the place along the through highway (st.sight_along_way), not as what the driver perceived.

With every entrance treated as stop-controlled, the through highway is read as any way the intersection lies on that the subject's approach carrier does not lie on; its legal designation is read from the scene.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.traffic_signal head, uncovered, governs intersection i and is dev.inoperative. x (a passenger car) occupies lane c with st.lane_enters c i; stop line s has st.entrance_of s c. x approaches from 60 m upstream at 10 m/s, slows to 3 m/s near s and enters i without kin.speed ever falling to the speed tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; x halts (kin.speed 0) with its front 0.5 m short of s, on c, then enters i.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal head governing i is operating (state circular_green, not dev.inoperative) when x enters i without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe dev.inoperative, so whether the signal was inoperative at the entry is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No stop line is recorded for c (association observed, empty); crosswalk w has st.entrance_of w c. x halts with its footprint overlapping w and then enters i.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Neither a stop line nor a crosswalk marks c (associations observed). x halts outside i, 1 m from its edge, where st.sight_along_way to the crossing highway is 120 m, then enters.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with x already on c within the stopping zone of s, rolling at 1 m/s; no halt is recorded before x enters the inoperative-signal intersection, and no approach start is visible.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start of x on c (its last observation outside the stopping zone of s), before the recording begins

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point tolerance of the approach convention: the distance between a road user's body and the governing mark (stop line, crosswalk or intersection edge) within which a halt counts as made at that mark, set from the spread of halting positions at stop-controlled approaches.
param_proposals.source: Observational studies of stopping position at stop-controlled approaches (FHWA/ITE stop-sign compliance studies)

param_proposals.name: p.approach_view_sight_distance
param_proposals.convention: Sight distance along a crossing way that gives a view of approaching traffic: the stopping sight distance at a 30 mph design speed.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance table

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)

segmentation.text: When a vehicle
enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered,
but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver
shall proceed
cautiously,
yielding to vehicles which have previously completed a stop or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'.
rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' on st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'; the entry is the observation at which the overlap last became true.

dev.traffic_signal 'a signal head' with the 'uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered'; dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection', the intersection or a carrier entering it (st.lane_enters).
dev.inoperative 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the entry observation through a past operator, the moment the words fix.
The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; the class is the vehicle aggregate.

'Such a stop' is the stop the sibling words require, with every qualification they keep: a halt (drv.motion.stopped, DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') made on x's approach carrier c (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c i, st.travel_region) before this entry and since the approach began, at the governing place - the st.stop_line marking c (st.entrance_of), else the st.crosswalk marking c with the footprint not overlapping it, else c's entrance end outside st.intersection where st.sight_along_way along a through st.highway (st.on_way) meets the view bound - within the stop-point tolerance of it (st.region_geometry) on its upstream side (prim.region_offset_along along c's direction).
The same driver, read through the vehicle's controlled motion; vehicle aggregate.
Proceeding is the subject's motion (drv.motion.moving, speed above the resolution) while its footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection), the entry included.

The vehicles yielded to (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle): a vehicle y that previously completed a stop halted (drv.motion.stopped, 'complete cessation from movement') on its own approach carrier cy whose entrance end is i (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters, st.travel_region), outside i, its halt beginning before x's halt on c (time since y's halt rose greater than time since x's); or a vehicle y whose footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection).

operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the subject proceeds cautiously, yielding, where it moves without creating a conflict with a vehicle it must yield to - no such vehicle whose centre and the subject's, under constant velocities, approach within the time-to-collision horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x's footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies) and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), where: at the entry of the current occupancy (the observation at which x's overlap with i last became true) at least one installed, uncovered traffic signal head governed i or a carrier entering i and every such head governing i or x's approach carrier was inoperative (read at that entry observation through a past operator); and x made such a stop before that entry: on its approach carrier c (the carrier with st.lane_enters c i x occupied at the observation before the entry), since its approach to the governing place began, x was halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance) at that place as NRS_484B_250_4_o1 reads it - the stop line marking c, else before the crosswalk marking c, else outside i at c's entrance end where st.sight_along_way along a through highway is at least p.approach_view_sight_distance - within p.stop_point_tolerance of it on its upstream side; and there is a vehicle y other than x such that (a) y's footprint overlaps i, or (b) y occupies a carrier cy whose entrance end is i, outside i, and halted on cy (drv.motion.stopped) since it last came onto cy, its halt beginning earlier than x's halt on c.
obligation: No vehicle y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection) has its centre and x's approach, under constant velocities, within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Cautiously' is read only through the yield the words attach to it: the subject does not move within the intersection into a predicted conflict with a vehicle it must yield to; no further speed or manner bound is read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Intersection i's only signal head is uncovered and dev.inoperative. x halts at the stop line of its approach lane c, then moves into i at 4 m/s while vehicle y, within i on the crossing way, crosses x's path; prim.closest_approach_distance is 1 m at 1.2 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but x moves into i only while y, still within i, is leaving on the far side: predicted closest approach 9 m.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing i shows circular_green (not inoperative) when x enters; x moves through i next to y.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but dev.inoperative is not observed, so the condition at the entry is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: y halted on its approach cy before x halted at its stop line; as x moves into i, y starts into i and their predicted closest approach is 0.8 m within 1.5 s.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x halts at its stop line, then moves through i with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but x never halted on c before entering (kin.speed stays above the tolerance): the condition 'after making such a stop' does not hold.

param_proposals.source: Observational studies of stopping position at stop-controlled approaches (FHWA/ITE stop-sign compliance studies)

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
approaching an intersection
shall yield
the right-of-way
to a vehicle which has entered the intersection
from a different highway.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: The driver of a vehicle: the vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); the driver role read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Approaching an intersection is occupying a carrier whose entrance end is that intersection: rel.occupies on a carrier c (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; 'a road user occupying one such carrier approaches through it whatever its motion'. Not the subject's presence in the intersection, which the obligation reads.

Yielding is not moving into the intersection (drv.motion.moving with rel.occupies of st.intersection) while the precedence of another vehicle is owed; the entry observation, where x's footprint overlaps both c and i, is where it is judged.

A vehicle y (vehicle aggregate) which has entered: y's footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) and has overlapped it continuously since an observation at which y occupied a carrier cy with st.lane_enters cy i, the carrier it entered from.

From a different highway: y's carrier cy lies on a st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') (st.on_way 'the public way ... a structure region lies on') that x's approach carrier c does not lie on.

An official traffic-control device (DEF-NRS-484A-145 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority') that controls an intersection: the words 'intersections controlled by' limit its members to the devices that assign precedence at the junction - dev.traffic_signal 'a signal head', dev.stop_sign 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt', dev.yield_sign 'regulatory sign requiring yielding' - that govern i or a carrier entering it (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'). Markings, warning and guide signs control no precedence at the junction and are left out. Official status read from presence.

Vehicles (aggregate) approaching from opposite directions: rel.oncoming's contract says the direction a road user approaches from is 'read through the carrier it approaches through ... and through that carrier's direction (st.lane_direction)'. x's approach carrier c and y's approach carrier cy (each with st.lane_enters into i, y's being the one it entered from) have designated directions (st.lane_direction 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') whose dot product is below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance.

Is making a left turn: the vehicle's heading is turning to the left (drv.motion.turning_left, yaw rate to the left above the resolution) while its footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash between x and y is a predicted closest approach of their centres, under constant velocities (which carry direction, speed and proximity), within the time-to-collision horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below the clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes a left turn at the target region.

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x occupies a carrier c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is an intersection i (st.lane_enters c i) - x approaching i, the observation of its entry, where its footprint overlaps both c and i, included - and there is a vehicle y other than x that has entered i from a different highway: y's footprint overlaps i and has overlapped it continuously since an observation at which y occupied a carrier cy with st.lane_enters cy i, cy lying on a highway (st.on_way) that c does not lie on. A y is not counted (exception) where x and y approach from opposite directions (dot product of st.lane_direction of c and cy below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance) and x or y has a declared intention to turn left at i (int.turn_left) or is turning left within i (drv.motion.turning_left with p.yaw_rate_tolerance). Not applicable where i is controlled by an official traffic-control device: a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs i or a carrier whose entrance end is i (dev.governs); this exception is suspended where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 or NRS_484B_250_4_o2 applies to x (an intersection whose signal is inoperative when x enters).
obligation: At a judged observation at which x's footprint overlaps i and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), no vehicle y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection and exception) has its centre and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
The official status of a signal or sign is read from its presence on the road.
Yielding is judged where x moves into or within the intersection; slowing on the approach before entry is not separately checked.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: No device governs i or its approaches. x approaches on lane c (st.lane_enters c i, on highway A); y entered i from lane cy on highway B and is crossing. x moves into i; predicted closest approach 1 m in 1.5 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but x halts on c while y crosses i and enters only after y has left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A dev.stop_sign governs c; the intersection is controlled by an official device and no signal is inoperative.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.lane_enters is not observed, so whether x approaches i and from which carrier y entered is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x and y approach on opposed carriers (dot product of directions -1); y has int.turn_left at i and is turning left within i when x moves in: y is excepted and no other vehicle has entered i.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: i is governed by a dev.traffic_signal that is dev.inoperative at x's entry; the device exception is suspended; y crossing from highway B, conflict predicted when x moves in.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: x approaches and enters an uncontrolled intersection with no other road user in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which two approach carriers' designated directions are still opposite directions (about 45 degrees), separating opposite approaches from crossing ones at junctions whose legs meet near right angles.
param_proposals.source: Intersection leg geometry convention (AASHTO Green Book: legs intersecting at angles near 90 degrees)

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)

param_proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Yaw-rate resolution: the noise floor of a source's yaw-rate estimate, below which a heading is read as not changing.
param_proposals.source: Yaw-rate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
which is within the intersection
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,

but such driver, having so yielded and having given a signal when and as required, may make such left turn and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection from the opposite direction shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: Vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'); the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' on st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'; the region the intention is declared at.
Yielding within the intersection is not moving (drv.motion.moving) there (rel.occupies, st.intersection) into a predicted conflict with a vehicle owed precedence.

Any vehicle y (aggregate) approaching from the opposite direction: per rel.oncoming's contract the approach direction is 'read through the carrier it approaches through ... and through that carrier's direction (st.lane_direction)'. y's approach carrier cy (occupied with st.lane_enters cy i, or for y within i the one it occupied when its current occupancy of i began) and x's approach carrier cx (the one x occupied when its current occupancy of i began) have designated directions with dot product below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance. A turn does not change the approach direction.
y's footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

operationalizations.standard: so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance: an approaching vehicle outside the intersection is an immediate hazard where its time to reach the intersection is at most the critical gap, i.e. its ground distance to the intersection (st.region_geometry) is at most its speed (kin.speed) times the critical gap; the bound moves with the vehicle's speed and distance.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes a left turn at the target region.

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x's footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies), the declaration current at that observation states that x intends to turn left at i (int.turn_left x i), and there is a vehicle y other than x approaching from the opposite direction - the designated direction (st.lane_direction) of y's approach carrier cy (a carrier y occupies with st.lane_enters cy i, or, for y within i, the carrier it occupied when its current occupancy of i began) and that of x's approach carrier cx (the carrier with st.lane_enters cx i that x occupied when its current occupancy of i began) have a dot product below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance - which either overlaps i (rel.occupies) or, outside i, has a ground distance to i (st.region_geometry) at most its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_time_gap.
obligation: Where x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), no vehicle y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection) has its centre and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Yielding is judged where x moves within the intersection; a stationary x yields.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield the right-of-way to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction which is within the intersection or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver,
having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles
approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: The left-turning party y is a vehicle: DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported').
y's footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', st.intersection); the region y's intention is declared at.

A signal of a left turn is sig.turn_indicator state left ('the left or the right one') or sig.hand_signal meaning left ('a driver's or rider's arm signal'); 'not a stand-in for the turn itself' respected - the signal is read as the signal. 'When and as required' points to signalling rules outside this corpus; carried as the words say: a left signal shown by y at some observation since it last came onto its approach carrier, continuing into the turn.
The other drivers are drivers of vehicles: the vehicle aggregate, the subject x, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

x approaches i through a carrier cx it occupies with st.lane_enters cx i ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into'); 'from the opposite direction' is read, per rel.oncoming's contract, through the carriers' designated directions: st.lane_direction of cx and of y's approach carrier cy have a dot product below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance.
Yielding is not moving into the intersection (drv.motion.moving with rel.occupies of st.intersection) while the turning vehicle's precedence is owed.
The vehicle making the left turn: y's heading is turning to the left (drv.motion.turning_left) while its footprint overlaps the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes a left turn at the target region.

residues.why: The permission to make the turn adds nothing to the condition: the vehicle yielded to is the one 'making the left turn' (s13), which already requires the turn under way.

applicability: x is a vehicle occupying a carrier cx with st.lane_enters cx i (approaching intersection i; its entry observation, overlapping both, included), and there is a vehicle y other than x such that: y's footprint overlaps i; the declaration current at the observation states y intends to turn left at i (int.turn_left y i); y's approach carrier cy (the carrier with st.lane_enters cy i it occupied when its current occupancy of i began) has a designated direction opposed to cx's (dot product of st.lane_direction below minus p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance); y has complied with NRS_484B_253_o1 (x of that rule mapped to y) at every observation since its current occupancy of i began; y showed a left signal (sig.turn_indicator left or sig.hand_signal left) at some observation since it last came onto cy; and y is turning left within i (drv.motion.turning_left with p.yaw_rate_tolerance).
obligation: At an observation at which x's footprint overlaps i and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), there is no vehicle y meeting every condition of the applicability (bound again with the whole selection) whose centres and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The drivers are read through the vehicles' controlled motion.
Yielding is judged where x moves into or within the intersection; slowing on the approach is not separately checked.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle

shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.

After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped, the driver shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: Traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') being controlled by a police officer: dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ... police_officer' governing (dev.governs) the approach carrier of x or the intersection i. The traffic controlled is the traffic on x's approach, x itself a member of it.

Traffic being controlled by a traffic-control signal (DEF-NRS-484A-290 'by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed'): a dev.traffic_signal head governing x's approach carrier or i (dev.governs) that is not dev.inoperative ('installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication') and not in state dark; an inoperative head directs nothing.

Proper signs are dev.stop_sign 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt' or dev.yield_sign 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt' governing (dev.governs) the carrier x approaches through (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) or the intersection; propriety and erection by authority are read from the sign's presence.
Vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Stop' when required is DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement' (drv.motion.stopped); 'yield' at the place, under a yield sign, is what the next sentence names, 'slowed or stopped': a halt or a speed (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity') at or below the yield-control check speed. The place, in order: st.stop_line 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device' recorded as marking x's carrier (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'); else st.crosswalk 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection' marking it, with the footprint not yet overlapping it (rel.occupies); else the carrier's entrance end at st.intersection, with the footprint outside it. At the place is within the stop-point tolerance (st.region_geometry body distance), upstream along the carrier's direction (prim.region_offset_along), on the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters, st.travel_region).

operationalizations.standard: has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway
operationalizations.convention: The view of approaching traffic on the through highway is a sight distance along that way (st.sight_along_way 'within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye') at least the stopping sight distance of the approach-speed design convention. The through highway is a st.highway the intersection lies on (st.on_way) and x's approach carrier does not: the way whose traffic the sign on x's approach makes x yield to (DEF-NRS-484A-275 'at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield').

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each entry of x into an intersection i (x's footprint overlaps i and did not at the observation before), where at the observation before the entry x occupied a carrier c (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters c i, and a stop sign or yield sign governs c or i (dev.governs). Not applicable where, at the entry observation, x's traffic is controlled by a police officer (a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs c or i) or by a traffic signal (a dev.traffic_signal governing c or i that is not dev.inoperative and not in state dark).
obligation: Event: the entry of x into i. Approach: the carrier c x occupies at the observation before the entry with st.lane_enters c i; where several such carriers give different verdicts, unknown. Act: where a stop sign governs c or i, a halt (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance); where only a yield sign governs, a halt or a speed (kin.speed) at or below p.yield_sign_check_speed. Place, in the words' order: (1) a stop line s recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of s c); (2) where c's stop-line association is observed and lists none, a crosswalk w recorded as marking c, the act made with x's footprint not overlapping w; (3) where neither is recorded (associations observed), the entrance end of c: with x's footprint outside i within p.stop_point_tolerance of i, at an observation at which st.sight_along_way from x to the through highway h (a st.highway i lies on and c does not, st.on_way) is at least p.approach_view_sight_distance. The act counts at an observation at which x is on c, outside i, on the upstream side of the place (prim.region_offset_along along c's designated direction, the place itself included) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry distance between x's body and the place). History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start (the last observation before the entry at which x, on a carrier the place marks, is short of the place and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance) or at x's previous entry into i through the same place. Met where the act is found; violated where the search reaches either end without it; unknown only where it reaches neither (the recording begins inside the stopping zone with no act recorded), and unknown where the carrier association, its direction or the sight distance is unobserved and the verdict turns on it.

narrowings.why: 'Proper signs ... erected' is read from the presence of a stop or yield sign governing the approach.
The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'Clearly marked' is read as the stop line the scene represents.

'Yield' at the place under a yield sign is read, by the words of the next sentence, as slowing to at most the yield-control check speed or halting there; 'the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view' is read as the entrance end of the approach carrier at which the view bound is met.
The driver's view is read as what could be seen from the place along the through way (st.sight_along_way), not as what the driver perceived.
The through highway's designation is read from the stop or yield sign governing the subject's approach: every way the intersection lies on that the approach carrier does not.

scenarios.boundary: the approach start of x on c (its last observation outside the stopping zone of s), before the recording begins

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield
the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way to that traffic until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: Vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes' (DEF-NRS-484A-060 'no legal right of access except at such points only'). 'About to' is an imminent movement, read by the movement it leads to: the entry (x's footprint begins to overlap the controlled-access region, rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region ... controlled-access lane') or the exit (it ceases to overlap it, onto another st.highway region).

Yielding is not making the entry or exit (the change of x's overlap with the controlled-access region, rel.occupies) while moving (drv.motion.moving) into a predicted conflict with a vehicle owed precedence.

All vehicles y (aggregate) approaching on the highway: y moving (drv.motion.moving) with its footprint on the highway being entered - the controlled-access region at an entry, the st.highway region x moves onto at an exit (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

operationalizations.standard: whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance for merging: a vehicle on the highway is an immediate hazard where the gap between the bodies (rel.surface_gap 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') is at most its speed (kin.speed) times the critical gap, so the bound moves with its speed.

applicability: x is a vehicle. segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield
the right-of-way
to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: Vehicle aggregate; the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes'; 'about to' read by the movement it leads to: entry into or exit from the controlled-access region (rel.occupies changing), onto another st.highway region at an exit.

The referent of 'that traffic': vehicles y (aggregate) moving (drv.motion.moving) on the highway being entered (rel.occupies of the controlled-access region at an entry, of the st.highway region x moves onto at an exit).
Continuing to yield is not making the entry or exit (x's overlap with the controlled-access region changing, rel.occupies) while moving (drv.motion.moving) before it may proceed safely.

'That traffic' (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') refers to the vehicles of s4-s5 whose proximity was an immediate hazard; the rule reads them as traffic members of the vehicle aggregate with every qualification s4-s5 state.

operationalizations.standard: whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance for merging: the body gap (rel.surface_gap) at most the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) times the critical gap.

Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.
Traffic-conflict technique: x may proceed with reasonable safety once no vehicle of that traffic has a predicted closest approach to x within the time-to-collision horizon below the centre clearance.

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each entry of x into a controlled-access region a (x's footprint overlaps a and did not at the observation before) and each exit (it no longer overlaps a and did at the observation before), where there is a vehicle y other than x of that traffic: at some observation of the run of observations immediately before that event during which x stayed on the near side (for an entry, off a; for an exit, on a), y was moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) on the highway being entered (a at an entry; at an exit, a st.highway region x's footprint overlaps at the exit, not a) with a body gap to x (rel.surface_gap) at most its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_time_gap.
obligation: Where x is moving at the event observation (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), no vehicle y of that traffic (bound again with its whole selection) has a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'About to enter or exit' is read by the movement it leads to: the entry into or exit from the controlled-access region.
'Reasonable safety' is read only as the absence of a predicted conflict with that traffic at the moment x proceeds; no other factor is read.

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
may proceed
with due care
on the immediately adjacent highway
to move around such an obstruction.
Such a pedestrian:
(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk
as possible;
(b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic;
(c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;
and (d) Must return to the sidewalk as soon as practicable.

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate', not expanded.

Walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk: the pedestrian moves (drv.motion.moving, 'in motion ... in any direction') with its footprint on st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (rel.occupies); not a crosswalk.

An obstruction to mobility is st.obstruction 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user' (kinds include sidewalk_fixture, excavation, barrier, debris); encountering it on the sidewalk is the pedestrian, on the sidewalk (rel.occupies st.sidewalk), coming within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of it (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), a reach relating a region to a road user.
Proceeding: the pedestrian moves on (drv.motion.moving) off the sidewalk; it marks the start of the detour.

On the immediately adjacent highway: the pedestrian's footprint overlaps the st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') that the sidewalk it left lies on (st.on_way), and no st.sidewalk.

To move around the obstruction is a purpose read through the conduct it explains: the detour episode, from the pedestrian leaving the sidewalk at an obstruction it encountered (within reach, st.region_geometry) until it is back on a sidewalk.
Such a pedestrian: the same pedestrian aggregate member, on its detour.

Walking or traveling on the highway during the detour (rel.occupies st.highway) as far to the side near the sidewalk: the ground distance from the pedestrian's body to the sidewalk it left (st.region_geometry, st.sidewalk).

A lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters is st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; the pedestrian's footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). The words name the lane's purpose, not road users of those classes, so no aggregate is claimed.

operationalizations.standard: as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk as possible
operationalizations.convention: Pedestrian facility design: a detouring pedestrian keeps as close to the sidewalk as possible where its body stays within one pedestrian width plus a shy distance of the sidewalk (st.region_geometry distance).

assumptions.meaning: A short section of the sidewalk on which the pedestrian is travelling is missing or cannot be passed on foot, at the place the pedestrian leaves it.
The area of the highway between the bicycle lane or path the pedestrian occupies and the adjacent sidewalk cannot be passed on foot at the observation.

residues.why: 'With due care' qualifies the permission to leave the sidewalk; the duty to keep to the side applies to such a pedestrian whether or not care was taken, so the words add no restriction to this duty.
Permission (b) concerns the direction of travel on the highway; the duty to keep to the side near the sidewalk is the same in either direction, so the words add no restriction to this duty.

applicability: x is a pedestrian. Judged at each observation of a detour: x's footprint overlaps a highway region h (st.highway) and no sidewalk, and x has been off every sidewalk continuously since an observation at which x was moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) on a sidewalk w lying on h (st.on_way w h), at which either an obstruction o (st.obstruction) was within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry) or asm.sidewalk_section_missing_or_impassable held. Not applicable (exception c) where x's footprint overlaps a bicycle lane or path (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) and asm.area_beside_bicycle_lane_impassable holds.
obligation: x's body is within p.pedestrian_detour_side_distance of the sidewalk w it left (st.region_geometry ground distance from x to w).

narrowings.why: The purpose of moving around the obstruction is read through the detour conduct: off the sidewalk since leaving it at an encountered obstruction.
'As possible' is read as a fixed lateral bound from the sidewalk; an obstruction that itself extends into the highway beyond that bound is not read.

who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,

may proceed
with due care

to move around such an obstruction.
Such a pedestrian:

(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk as possible; (b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic; (c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;
and (d) Must return to the sidewalk
as soon as practicable.

elements.justification: Pedestrian aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...').
Moving (drv.motion.moving) with the footprint on st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (rel.occupies).

st.obstruction 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user' within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of the pedestrian's body (st.region_geometry) while it is on the sidewalk (rel.occupies).
Proceeding: the pedestrian moves on (drv.motion.moving) off the sidewalk; the detour episode.
The pedestrian's footprint on the st.highway the sidewalk lies on (st.on_way), and on no st.sidewalk.
Purpose read through conduct: the detour about the encountered obstruction (st.region_geometry distance to it).
The same pedestrian on its detour.
Returning to the sidewalk: the pedestrian's footprint overlaps a st.sidewalk again (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.convention: Walking-time convention: once clear of the obstruction (farther than the encounter reach from every obstruction, st.region_geometry), a pedestrian can step back onto the sidewalk within the time needed to walk a few metres at the design walking speed; staying off the sidewalk (rel.occupies of st.sidewalk false) and clear of every obstruction for longer than that time (a .time window, kin.time) is not as soon as practicable.

assumptions.meaning: A short section of the sidewalk on which the pedestrian is travelling is missing or cannot be passed on foot, at the place the pedestrian leaves it.

residues.why: 'With due care' qualifies the permission to leave the sidewalk; the duty to return applies to such a pedestrian whether or not care was taken, so the words add no restriction to this duty.

applicability: x is a pedestrian. Judged at each observation of a detour: x's footprint overlaps a highway region h (st.highway) and no sidewalk, and x has been off every sidewalk continuously since an observation at which x was moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) on a sidewalk w lying on h (st.on_way w h), at which either an obstruction (st.obstruction) was within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry) or asm.sidewalk_section_missing_or_impassable held.
obligation: It is not the case that, at every observation of the time window of length p.sidewalk_return_time behind the judged observation, x's footprint overlapped no sidewalk and x's body was farther than p.obstruction_encounter_reach from every obstruction (st.region_geometry); a window reaching before the start of the recording is unknown.

narrowings.why: The purpose of moving around the obstruction is read through the detour conduct.

'As soon as practicable' is read from the moment the pedestrian is clear of every obstruction; where the detour was triggered only by the declared missing or impassable section, being clear of it is read as being clear of every obstruction object.

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding a bicycle,
an electric bicycle
or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]
on the pathway or lane.

The driver of a motor vehicle shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway; (b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle; (c) To avoid conflict with other traffic; (d) In the performance of official duties; (e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer; or (f) In an emergency.

Yielding on the pathway or lane is not moving (drv.motion.moving) with the footprint on the bicycle lane or path (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path) into a predicted conflict with a road user owed precedence there.
A person riding a bicycle: DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), the ridden road user.
DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts').
DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on').
DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...'), limited by s8 to a pedestrian in the situation subsection 6 provides for.

On the pathway or lane: the road user yielded to has its footprint on st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them' (rel.occupies).

applicability: x is a motor vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x's footprint overlaps a bicycle lane or path b (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path) and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), where there is a road user y other than x whose footprint overlaps b and which is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter), or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) to which NRS_484B_297_6_o2 applies (its x mapped to y: a pedestrian on a detour around a sidewalk obstruction).
obligation: No road user y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection) has its centre and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

Yielding is judged where the motor vehicle moves with its footprint on the pathway or lane; slowing before reaching it is not separately checked.

The driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
except:
(a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;
(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;
(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;
(d) In the performance of official duties;
(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;
or (f) In an emergency.

elements.justification: Motor vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Entering, stopping, standing, parking and driving within a region jointly cover every observation at which the vehicle's footprint overlaps it, moving or halted (DEF-NRS-484A-260 stop 'any halting, even momentarily'; DEF-NRS-484A-250 stand 'the halting of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-155 park 'the standing of a vehicle'): rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. The definitions' own exclusions (a halt to avoid conflict or on an officer's direction) coincide with exceptions (c) and (e). A pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters is st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; the words name the lane's purpose, not road users, so no aggregate is claimed.

Entering or exiting an alley or driveway: during x's current stay on the lane (the run of observations its footprint overlaps it), x's footprint overlaps a st.driveway_or_alley_entrance 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway' or a st.alley 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties' (rel.occupies) - at an observation before in the stay (exiting) or after it in the stay (entering).

To avoid conflict with other traffic is a purpose read through the conduct it explains: at the observation at which x's current stay on the lane began, some road user z other than x that is traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway') and not on the lane had a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

In compliance with the directions of a police officer: a dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic and the direction given' with role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a region x's footprint overlaps at the observation; x's presence in the lane is read as following that direction.

assumptions.meaning: The road user's vehicle is disabled: it cannot proceed under its own power at the observation.
The road user is engaged in the performance of official duties at the observation.
An emergency is in progress for the road user at the observation.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle. Judged at every observation. Where x's footprint overlaps a bicycle lane or path b, not applicable where any exception holds at the observation: (a) during x's current stay on b, x's footprint overlaps a driveway or alley entrance or an alley at some observation of the stay; (b) asm.vehicle_disabled; (c) at the observation at which the current stay on b began, a road user z other than x that is traffic and not on b had a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance; (d) asm.performing_official_duties; (e) a police officer's direction (dev.human_direction role police_officer) governs a region x's footprint overlaps; (f) asm.emergency. Where x's footprint overlaps no bicycle lane or path, no exception is read and the rule applies.
obligation: x's footprint overlaps no bicycle lane or path (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

The five acts are read jointly as the footprint overlapping the lane; the exclusion in the definition of stopping of a halt in compliance with an official traffic-control device is not read (such a halt within the lane is still driving within it).
The purpose of avoiding conflict is read through a predicted conflict with other traffic at the moment the vehicle moved onto the lane.
Compliance with the officer's direction is read as an officer's direction governing the region the vehicle is in.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x drives 50 m along bicycle lane b mid-block; no driveway or alley, no officer, no conflict at entry; the trace declares asm.vehicle_disabled, asm.performing_official_duties and asm.emergency false.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x drives in the general lane next to b, never overlapping b.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x crosses b to turn into a driveway: during the stay its footprint overlaps a st.driveway_or_alley_entrance.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.occupies is not observed, so whether x is on b is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x drives in b while a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs b and directs traffic through it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x swerves onto b at the moment a vehicle merging from the left has a predicted closest approach to x of 1 m in 1 s.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3 [NRS-484B-270-3],
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter or proceed through an intersection
while driving within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters.

elements.justification: Motor vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Entering or proceeding through an intersection: the observation at which x's footprint begins to overlap st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet' (rel.occupies true here, false at the observation before); proceeding through begins with that entry.

Driving within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters: x moving (drv.motion.moving) with its footprint on st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them' (rel.occupies); the words name the lane's purpose, not road users, so no aggregate is claimed.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) with its footprint on a bicycle lane or path (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path), and where NRS_484B_270_3_o2 applies to x (its x mapped to x): none of subsection 3's exceptions (a)-(f) excuses x's presence in the lane.
obligation: x does not enter an intersection at the judged observation: it is not the case that x's footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies, st.intersection) and did not at the observation before.

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'Proceed through' is read at the entry into the intersection, where every passage through it begins.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x drives in bicycle lane b up to intersection i and its footprint enters i while still on b; no exception holds and the trace declares asm.vehicle_disabled, asm.performing_official_duties and asm.emergency false.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x drives in b mid-block (no exception holds) and does not enter an intersection while in it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x enters i from a general traffic lane, never on a bicycle lane or path.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.occupies is not observed, so neither the bicycle-lane occupancy nor the entry can be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs b and directs x through it: subsection 3's exception (e) holds, so NRS_484B_270_3_o2 does not apply.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)

contract: A road user is at a complete halt at the observation: the definition's "complete cessation from movement", observed as the magnitude of its velocity (kin.speed) at or below `tol`, a tolerance that names only the source's speed resolution, below which a sampled speed counts as no movement. It denotes the halt whoever or whatever controls the road user. Not denoted: a halt held over a window, since the concept reads the one observation; where the road user halts, which the caller states.

params.name: tol
params.meaning: the source's speed resolution: a speed at or below it is read as no movement

elements.span: the magnitude of its velocity (kin.speed) at or below `tol`
elements.justification: kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity'; the definition's absolute 'complete cessation from movement' is observed over sampled speeds within the resolution tol.

residues.why: The definition's scope ('when required'): which duty requires the halt is the caller's, not the concept's.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x's kin.speed is 0.05 m/s with tol 0.2 m/s: halted.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x's kin.speed is 2 m/s: moving, not halted.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: kin.speed is not observed for x.

contract: A road user's heading is turning to the left at the observation: its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, positive to the left, counter-clockwise) exceeds `tol`, a tolerance that names only the source's yaw-rate resolution, whether the road user moves forwards or backwards. Not denoted: a heading turning to the right or not changing; the angle turned or a completed turn; where the turn is made, which the caller states. The concept does not tell a turn at a junction from a lane change or a bend; the caller's place condition does.

params.name: tol
params.meaning: the source's yaw-rate resolution: a yaw rate at or below it is read as no turning to the left

elements.span: its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, positive to the left, counter-clockwise) exceeds `tol`
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)'; its exclusion 'not a stand-in for road curvature' is respected: the concept states a heading change, not a road shape, and leaves the place to the caller.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x's kin.yaw_rate is +12 deg/s with tol 2 deg/s: turning left.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x's kin.yaw_rate is -12 deg/s: turning right.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: kin.yaw_rate is not observed for x.

differs_from.why: drv.motion.turning reads the magnitude of the yaw rate, a turn to either hand; this concept reads its sign, a turn to the left only.
